ShouldFadeAfterDeath.rationale: Presentation, and EXECUTED rather than reflex-waived: `grep -rn ShouldFadeAfterDeath src/` resolves exactly one reader, NCreature.cs:697 (`monster.ShouldFadeAfterDeath && Body.IsVisibleInTree()`), inside the Godot death-animation node. TakeDamageSfxType.rationale: DamageSfxType.Magic. Presentation (SHARED-FINDINGS section 4, matching monster_state_machine N2/N5).

AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: READ TO THE END before waiving (the KinPriest N6 lesson). SoulNexus.cs:43-47 awaits base.AfterAddedToRoom() -- a no-op on the base class (MonsterModel.cs:313-316) -- and then subscribes a private handler to Creature.Died. That handler (SoulNexus.cs:49-53) unsubscribes itself and sets the creature node's spine animation to 'tracks/empty'. There is NO mechanical effect anywhere in the pair, so unlike every other unit in this batch SoulNexus applies no starting power and SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 does not apply to it: `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py ctor-order` does not list soul_nexus among the 35 constructor-applying monsters.

BeforeRemovedFromRoom.rationale: SoulNexus.cs:55-61 -- the same 'tracks/empty' spine animation, guarded by !RunState.IsGameOver. Presentation.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node for node against SoulNexus.cs:63-78. Three MoveStates (SOUL_BURN_MOVE 29, MAELSTROM_MOVE 6x4, DRAIN_LIFE_MOVE 18 + Vulnerable 2 + Weak 2) all pointing their FollowUpState at one RandomBranchState 'RAND', which is added to the state list and is NOT the initial state; the initial state is SOUL_BURN_MOVE. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b08.py graphs`): sim prints SOUL_BURN_MOVE -> RAND, MAELSTROM_MOVE -> RAND, DRAIN_LIFE_MOVE -> RAND, initial=SOUL_BURN_MOVE. Ids match the C# exactly, so SHARED-FINDINGS section 3's rename allowance is not even needed.

ShouldShowMoveInBestiary.rationale: SoulNexus.cs:107-110 hides MAELSTROM_MOVE from the Bestiary list. Presentation; the sim has no Bestiary (monster_state_machine N5).

guards.what: THE CONTROL-MONSTER CHECK: SoulNexus.cs:70-72's three AddBranch calls (PROMPT.md bug class 6 / monster_state_machine G1's class)
guards.rationale: All three are `AddBranch(state, MoveRepeatType.CannotRepeat, 1f)` = overload #5 (RandomBranchState.cs:85, `MoveRepeatType repeatType, float weight`), which takes NO int argument at all. There is therefore no maxRepeats and no cooldown for a positional transliteration to convert into a weight, which is why this monster cannot exhibit G1's bug even in principle. The port (soul_nexus.py:52-54) passes `weight=1.0, repeat_type=MoveRepeatType.CANNOT_REPEAT` by KEYWORD and leaves max_times=0, cooldown=0 at their defaults. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b08.py soul-nexus-control`): every branch resolves to weight=1.0 cannot_repeat max_times=0 cooldown=0, and a 100000-roll distribution at seed 7 gives SOUL_BURN 33.4% / MAELSTROM 33.2% / DRAIN_LIFE 33.3%, which is the exact steady state of 'uniform over the two moves that are not the one just logged'. THE SEAM'S G4 CONTROL READING HOLDS, and this record confirms it without re-verdicting G4: with CannotRepeat the repeat window is n = 1 (RandomBranchState.cs:142-157, state_machine.py:201-204), so appending a duplicate to the tail of the log cannot move any weight. EXECUTED in the same probe: state_log [SOUL_BURN] gives weights [0.0, 1.0, 1.0] and state_log [SOUL_BURN, SOUL_BURN] gives the identical [0.0, 1.0, 1.0]. SoulNexus is correctly ported AND insensitive to G4's log-duplicate observable, exactly as monster_state_machine.md's G4 section claims.

guards.what: Branch ADD ORDER (observable: RandomBranchState.cs:115-128 resolves ties toward the earlier branch)
guards.rationale: C# adds SOUL_BURN, then MAELSTROM, then DRAIN_LIFE (SoulNexus.cs:70,71,72). The sim's `for move in (soul_burn, maelstrom, drain)` (soul_nexus.py:52) produces the same order; the probe prints the resolved branch list in add order and it matches. This matters because the walk subtracts weights in add order and returns the first branch reaching num <= 0, so with equal weights the order is part of the RNG mapping and not just cosmetic.

guards.what: DrainLifeMove's three sub-effects and their ORDER (SoulNexus.cs:98-105)
guards.rationale: C#: DamageCmd.Attack(18) -> PowerCmd.Apply<VulnerablePower>(targets, 2) -> PowerCmd.Apply<WeakPower>(targets, 2). soul_nexus.py:63-68 does the same three in the same order against ctx.player. C#'s applier is base.Creature at both apply sites; the sim passes none, so PowerCmd.apply's default of None is used (cmds.py:271-277). That matters only to listeners keyed on the applier, and neither VulnerablePower nor WeakPower has one -- unlike The Lost, whose record DOES need the explicit applier because PossessStrengthPower's tracker keys on it. Numbers checked against the non-ascension branch: SoulBurnDamage GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 31, 29) = 29, MaelstromDamage (7, 6) = 6, MaelstromRepeat (4, 4) = 4, DrainLifeDamage (19, 18) = 18, both power amounts literal 2m.

guards.what: Multi-hit MAELSTROM (6 x 4) through _execute_attack vs AttackCommand's hit loop
guards.rationale: monsters/base.py:107-118 `_execute_attack` fires before_attack, loops `hits` times through DamageCmd.deal and breaks when the player or the attacker is dead; then after_attack. C#'s AttackCommand.Execute (AttackCommand.cs:528-546) has the same two loop guards -- `if (Attacker.IsDead) break;` and an empty alive-target list -- and the sim's single target IS the player, so the two loops agree hit for hit. The one asymmetry is C#'s PRE-loop `if (Attacker.IsDead) return this;` (AttackCommand.cs:528-531), which also skips Hook.BeforeAttack; the sim has no such pre-guard. Unreachable for this unit and EXECUTED rather than asserted (rule 5): a sim monster can only take a turn while dead if `retained_after_death` is set (combat.py:292, :306), that flag is written only where hooks.should_remove_from_combat_after_death returns False (cmds.py:102-104, :200-202), and `grep -rn 'def should_remove_from_combat_after_death' sts2_rl/` returns exactly two sites -- the hook itself (hooks.py:603) and ReattachPower (powers.py:2338), which this monster never holds.

guards.what: Intent mapping: SingleAttackIntent / MultiAttackIntent / DebuffIntent(strong: true)
guards.rationale: The sim collapses C#'s AbstractIntent[] into one Intent with an `also` tuple (monsters/base.py:36-59). SOUL_BURN -> Intent(ATTACK, damage=29); MAELSTROM -> Intent(ATTACK, damage=6, hits=4); DRAIN_LIFE -> Intent(ATTACK, damage=18, also=(DEBUFF_STRONG,)) for C#'s [SingleAttackIntent(18), DebuffIntent(strong: true)]. Every number in the C# intent list survives the collapse for this unit. (The intent vocabulary itself is in no seam's scope -- monster_state_machine boundary item 2 -- so this is a unit-level check.)

SoulNexusElite.cs generates exactly one SoulNexus with a null slot and RoomType.Elite; the sim's SOUL_NEXUS_ELITE (soul_nexus.py:71-74) is the same single-monster encounter, registered as Glory's elite key `soul_nexus` (monsters/glory/__init__.py:74) and listed in rooms.py:195 elite_keys. Both sides reachable.
